guide.subtitle: Best Use of Flynet
guide.description: Build something that earns a place in someone’s next night out. Blackbird’s track is for apps and agents that put Flynet’s restaurant network, member data, or $FLY payments to useful work.

runs.text: Help someone find their next spot, make more of their dining history, or pay for an experience. Pick a specific problem and build a working flow with Flynet.

Flynet opens Blackbird’s dining network to developers. Its tools cover restaurant and location discovery, authenticated member profiles and check-ins, and $FLY payments. You can build an app, an agent, or a focused tool for diners or merchants.
Keep the scope small enough to demonstrate from start to finish. Flynet should make the product meaningfully better, and your demo should make that connection easy to see.
These are starting points. Bring your own idea if you see a better use for the network.

items.text: A dinner concierge that turns a request like “somewhere nearby for four people, open late” into a useful shortlist using restaurant details, locations, and hours.
A dining passport that helps a member revisit favorite places, see where they’ve been, and discover gaps in their own neighborhood map.
A plan for a night out that connects a few restaurants or bars on Flynet, with venue details and opening hours people can actually use.
A checkout flow that lets a Blackbird member pay with $FLY. Show the amount, request confirmation, and give them a clear payment result.
A discovery tool with a point of view: an occasion, a cuisine, a neighborhood, or a better way to explore the restaurant network.

runs.text: Start with discovery if your idea only needs restaurant and location data. Add member authentication when you need someone’s profile or visit history. Payment integrations require the appropriate partner access.
Follow the Flynet getting started guide and request staging access
Request access early. If you’re waiting on credentials, post in the Runtime Discord and say you’re building for the Blackbird / Flynet track. State which API access you need.

Once you have access, get one authenticated request working before building the rest of the product. The TypeScript SDK, @flynetdev/core, supports API calls; @flynetdev/react provides components for discovery and member experiences.
Use Flynet’s AI setup for Claude Code, Cursor, MCP servers, and agent skills
Keep API keys and client secrets on your server. Use a member’s authorized access for their personal data. In your demo, make clear which parts use staging data and which are live.

items.text: A clear reason to use it. Show who the product helps and how it improves a real dining or commerce experience.
A meaningful Flynet integration. Explain which data or payment tools you use and how they affect what the user can do.
A complete interaction. Let someone get from their initial request to a useful result, with sensible handling for missing data or a failed request.
An idea with some character. A focused product with a thoughtful interaction is easier to understand than a large collection of unfinished features.
Choose Blackbird under Sponsor track prizes in the Runtime submission form. Every submission is automatically eligible for the Bankr grand prize, and you can opt in to other tracks too.
Share your project link and describe the problem it solves, the Flynet APIs or SDK features you used, and the part that works today.
Walk through one complete user flow in your demo. Point out the Flynet integration and identify any mocked steps or test data.
Online submissions must include a viewable recorded demo. If you demo in person, a recording is strongly encouraged so reviewers can revisit the build.
Include a repository or technical walkthrough if it helps reviewers understand the integration. Keep credentials out of every shared link.
